findings.problem: Query, key and value are the heart of the video but the scene never says what they are. The row labels read only 'query', 'key', 'value', caption 1 is 'Each word makes a query, a key and a value.', and the number pairs (2 1 / 1 0 ...) appear from nowhere. A first-time learner can follow the arithmetic but not why there are three lists, what 'matching' means or why 'dog' wins. Scene 4 taught purple = the word asking, but what a KEY is (what a word offers to be matched) is never said, and 'value' only gets a meaning in scene 6 ('its content'). This is the house rule 'define jargon on screen before use' broken in the central scene.
findings.fix: Give each role one plain phrase on screen while its row pops in (1.0 to 3.0 s). For example split caption 1 in two: 'A query asks: what am I looking for?' (1.0 to 2.2) and 'A key says: this is what I offer.' (2.3 to 3.4), leaving 'value' to scene 6. Or slide three small 28 px tags in beside the row labels ('asks', 'offers', 'hands over'). Shorten the 0.55 s per-word stagger if time is tight. Also say once that this is a tiny new sentence, for example a grey tag 'tiny sentence' above the three word tags.
findings.evidence: s5@1.4 and s5@2.6 (rows labelled only query / key / value); caption list of scene 5 in algo-10.json.

findings.problem: German words (Ich, Wir, Das, Es ...) appear out of nowhere: the English sentence being translated is never shown (lesson 10.7's own card says 'toy scores for translating "I have eaten an apple" into German'). A first-time learner sees a model producing German at random and cannot tell why 'Ich' beats 'Wir' or why <eos> follows 'gegessen'. 'Writes' is also ambiguous without a source.
findings.fix: Show the source from 0.2 s: a grey tag 'I have eaten an apple' at the top of the stage (stage y 0, the slot row starts at y 120 so there is room) with a small orange label or arrow 'into German' pointing down at the slot row. Keep it to the end. No cross-attention drawing is needed (it is out of scope).
findings.evidence: s9@1.1, s9@4.0, s9@12.6 (no source anywhere); lesson text in js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-04.js line 88.

findings.problem: Rounds 3 to 6 (einen, Apfel, gegessen, <eos>; ROUND t0 = 9.2, 10.1, 10.9, 11.7) last only 0.8 to 0.9 s each. The candidate list is fully grown for about 0.3 s before the next round replaces it, so Kuchen / Hund / Tisch / gesehen / und / dann cannot be read. The caption 'Append the word, then go round again.' (9.8 to 11.6) is not drawn: a new word just pops into a slot while a fresh list appears, with nothing carrying the written word back to the 'next word?' question. The loop arrow only appears in the recap (row 3), so the idea is introduced after it is needed.
findings.fix: Give each of rounds 3 to 5 about 1.2 s: take about 0.6 s from the mask beat (arcs and grid hold about 2.6 s) and about 0.8 s from the 1.4 s end hold, keeping the video at or below 130 s. Draw the loop once on round 3: a green L5.arrow with a bow from the newly written slot back to the 'next word?' tag, drawn on as the word is written (reuse the recap's loop arrow idea), then flash it on rounds 4 to 6.
findings.evidence: s9@10.3, s9@11.0, s9@11.9 (a different list every 0.8 s); ROUND table in scene-09-decoder.js lines 62-67; s11@5.5 (loop arrow first seen in the recap).

findings.problem: The last beat ('Every word does this, all at the same time.', 9.4 to 12 s) is a tangle: 8 green arcs plus 6 self-loops piled under the sentence, crossing and overlapping (the 'robot' hub, a double arc between 'detected' and 'danger'). The tag says '7 × 7 = 49 shares' but nothing on screen can be counted to 49, and the 'it' row just explained is no longer part of it. The sentence sits at stage y 330, so the top 40 % of the stage is empty in this beat and the picture is bottom-heavy. It is the bridge to the 3 × 3 grid of scene 6, but it does not look like a grid.
findings.fix: Replace the arc web by a 7 × 7 heat grid (A10.grid, rows = word looking, columns = word looked at, shade from A10.ATT.w, no numbers) that fills row by row about 0.12 s apart, with the sentence words as row and column tags, the 'it' row ringed purple and '7 × 7 = 49 shares' beneath. Or keep arcs but show them for two words only. Centre the final picture vertically either way.

findings.problem: The tag above the bars switches to 'exponentiated' at 2.9 s. It is jargon, never defined, and not the caption's word ('Stretch the scores'). The step itself is a black box: bar C goes from 0 to 1.00, B from 1 to 2.72, A from 2 to 7.39 with no hint of the rule, so 'zero becomes one' looks like a mistake.
findings.fix: Change the tag to 'stretched' (matching the caption) and show the rule while the bars grow: 28 px tags 'e^2', 'e^1', 'e^0' beside the three numbers as they change, then fade them, plus one short word such as 'always positive'. If the caret is unwelcome, use the tag 'e to the score'.

findings.problem: Beat 2 (4.0 to 8.0 s) introduces two symbols that are never defined: the blue row is 'x' and the orange row 'adds F(x)'. A first-time learner cannot tell that x is the layer's input and F(x) is what attention produced, and the orange skip arc (from the bottom of Attention to Add & Norm) looks like a connector, not a bypass. The two ideas of the beat get about 3.5 s of picture (add 5.0 to 6.0, norm 6.4 to 7.4), and the caption for the second, 'Norm keeps the numbers steady.', is vague: the picture shows the mean line sliding to 0 and the bars re-centring.
findings.fix: Rename the tags in plain words: 'input' (replacing 'x'), 'from attention' (replacing 'adds F(x)'), 'input + attention' (replacing 'x + F(x)'); keep the numbers 1 3 5 7 / 2 −1 0.5 −2 / 3 2 5.5 5. Lift the skip arc over the Attention block (a bypass above the strip) instead of under it. Change caption 4 to 'Norm re-centres the numbers around zero.' and hold the norm view about 0.5 s longer (take the time from the end holds of scenes 3 or 5).
findings.evidence: s8@4.5 (tags 'x' / 'adds F(x)'), s8@5.3, s8@6.8 (bars already normalised while the numbers still read 3 2 5.5 5), s8@7.5.

findings.problem: Caption 1 says 'A layer has two main parts.' while four boxes sit on screen (Attention, Add & Norm, Feed-forward, Add & Norm), so a learner counts four. The headline 'Each layer mixes words, then thinks about each' also ends on a dangling 'each'.
findings.fix: Caption 1: 'Two parts, each wrapped in Add & Norm.' (7 words). Headline line 2: 'then thinks about each one' (about 800 px, fits the 936 px width).
findings.evidence: s8@1.2 (four boxes under the caption 'A layer has two main parts.').

findings.problem: The caption 'Nothing says which one came first.' (6.5 to 8.2 s) is carried by a lone orange question mark under the second 'the' column (stage x 528). Nothing links the two 'bank' columns, so the mark reads as a question about 'the', not about order; 'which came first' is never depicted.
findings.fix: Draw a dashed orange line joining the two 'same' tags (from x 309 to x 747 at y 321) with the question mark sitting on its middle, or better swap the two bank columns for 0.8 s (they exchange places and nothing changes, because the numbers are identical) so the learner sees that order cannot be detected.

findings.problem: The key operation of the scene, adding the position strip to the meaning strip (10.0 to 11.3 s), is its least legible moment. At 10.2 the orange strips slide over the blue ones, at 10.5 only orange numbers show (the blue ones are hidden underneath), then the cells flip to the sums and at 10.8 columns 4 to 6 are squashed to slivers with unreadable digits. No sum is ever shown as a calculation, so the learner has to trust that 0.7 + 0.8 = 1.5.
findings.fix: Before the slide, spend about 1 s on one worked column: ring the top cells of the first bank's blue and orange strips and show a tag '0.7 + 0.8 = 1.5' in the free band under the strips (y 292 to 350), then slide all columns together. Make the flip a cross-fade (no horizontal squash) so digits stay readable, and keep both strips visible 0.3 s longer.

findings.problem: Each token shows 4 numbers with no cue that these are the first 4 of 8 (and later scenes talk about 16 and 64 numbers per word). A first-time learner may think a token is exactly 4 numbers.
findings.fix: Add a 28 px grey '…' under each meaning strip (y about 282) or a tag 'first 4 of many numbers' near the first strip.

findings.problem: The share bar's three green segments are not tied to the words A, B and C (no letters, same colour) and the scene is an island: nothing says why softmax is needed (attention uses it two scenes later).
findings.fix: Put A, B, C in the segments (or tint them to match the discs) and end the last caption with 'We use this inside attention.' or add a tiny orange tag 'used by attention' at the end.

findings.problem: A small green loop appears on 'it' at 5.5 s (it looks at itself) with no caption or hint, and the headline says 'every other word' while the picture includes the word itself.
findings.fix: Caption 2: 'It looks at every word, itself included.' (7 words), or headline 'Every word looks at all the words'.

findings.problem: Colour roles slip. Scene 4 draws the new 'it' as a purple solid tag, but scene 6 draws the new 'barked' green (the video says a new vector is green). Scene 8's attention block and arcs are purple while attention arcs in scenes 4, 7 and 9 are green and purple means 'query'.
findings.fix: Make 'new “it”' (scene 4) a green solid tag, and draw the scene 8 attention arcs green (and the Attention block blue-grey or green tinted), keeping purple for the asking word only.

findings.problem: Caption 2 'Hold the query of “barked” against each key.' is an odd idiom for a first-time learner, and the scene switches from the robot sentence to 'the dog barked' without saying so.
findings.fix: 'Compare the query of “barked” with each key.' (9 words).

findings.problem: In the mask beat the red arcs fan out and stop in mid-air with crosses floating well above the empty slots, and the 7 × 7 grid has no meaning cue (which axis is the word looking?). The empty slots are also drawn at the width of the word that will fill them (the 'gegessen' slot is visibly wide), which hints that the sentence is planned in advance.
findings.fix: End each red arc on its own ghost slot with the cross on the slot's top edge; label the grid's left edge with a small arrow 'looks at' or ring the 'habe' row as now and add a 'habe' row tag; draw all ghost slots at one equal width.

findings.problem: '196 × 196' is a solid green square, so 'every token scores every token' (a table of pairs) is not drawn, and the cost lesson ('attention work grows with the square of the tokens') is only implied by the red colour at the end.
findings.fix: Draw faint grid lines on the square (for example 4 × 4) from the start so the shrink to one of 16 blocks reads clearly, and add a closing caption or tag such as 'Cost grows with the square.' in the last 1.5 s.

findings.problem: The tag '0.97' on the 'it to robot' arc is unlabelled (the word 'share' is not on screen) and the round Q / K / V chips use letters that scene 5 never showed (it used the full words).
findings.fix: Tag text 'share 0.97' (about 190 px wide) and use 'query', 'key', 'value' in a caption-linked way, or keep the letters but let the first caption say 'Q, K and V: each head has its own query, key and value.'

findings.problem: The word tags in scenes 2 and 5 and the Add & Norm strip in scene 8 start flush at stage y 0, so there is no 12 px margin to the stage top and they sit only about 27 px under the two-line headline text.
findings.fix: Shift those figures down by 12 px (scene 5 and 8 have room; scene 2's 'slot' tags already end at y 630, so shrink the strip gaps by 2 px per row there).
findings.evidence: s2@4.0, s5@2.6, s8@1.2 (a frame scan found the text of these tags at y 271 against a limit of 273).
